question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> mole of ideal gas is allowed to expand reversibly and adiabatically from a temperature of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The work done is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The final temperature of the gas is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> (Nearest integer). Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>

solution.text:
From first law of thermodynamics:
∆U = q + W
We know for adiabatic process,
∴q=0

∴ΔU=w⇒m × Cv × ∆T = w

⇒1×20×T2-300=-3000

⇒T2-300=-150

∴T2=150 K
